component.name: Pinto Slicer
component.summary: Prepare, support, slice, and export resin 3D prints

description.p: Pinto Slicer is a Linux-first resin 3D printer slicer built with Rust, egui, and wgpu. It provides a graphical workspace and command-line tools for preparing models and exporting native printer jobs.

ul.li: Move, rotate, scale, mirror, align, and arrange STL and OBJ models
Generate configurable automatic supports with presets
Inspect sliced exposure masks with layer playback
Save self-contained projects with embedded meshes
Export twelve job formats at native printer panel resolutions

description.p: Printer files have software-level validation, but physical-printer interoperability has not been verified. Run a small test print before starting a long job.

screenshot.caption: Automatic support generation on the build plate

description.p: The first public release of Pinto Slicer, with packages for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

ul.li: Interactive model preparation and automatic support generation
Layer preview, project files, and native printer-job export
Linux AppImage and Flatpak, universal macOS DMG, and portable Windows ZIP

description.p: The backlight now follows the real zone map, and the projection switch is easier to read.

ul.li: HALOT-X1 job files use the printer's exact 522-zone subzone map and enable every zone that covers a lit pixel.
The support-area projection experiment was removed; the slice image drives the backlight mask.
The viewport projection switch is a small Perspective | Orthographic tab pair instead of icons.

description.p: The backlight now follows each layer's real footprint, and the viewport's corner controls are quieter.

ul.li: HALOT-X1 job files light only the LED zones each slice covers, computed from the printer's own honeycomb geometry.
Support tips stop short of piercing thin walls.
The orientation cube's home button and the Persp/Ortho chips are clean icons instead of labelled boxes.

description.p: Fixes a print failure where parts cured only in the center, and brings supports in line with the printer's own slicer.

ul.li: The backlight now lights every zone so the whole model cures edge to edge.
Thinner, more numerous supports with a single welded raft sheet under each island.

description.p: Support columns now stand the way the printer's own slicer shapes them: cones, fat at the platform, slim where they meet the model.

ul.li: Standing trunks are about 5 mm wide at the foot, four times stiffer where columns are longest.
Trunks held from the model stay straight sticks, and the panel previews show the new shape.

description.p: The failed prints had one thing in common: a base sheet the size of the piece under them.

ul.li: No support pad may become a sheet: past the cap, the pad is cut with a drainable seam between the halves.
The pad rim keeps its full thickness and the middle sits lower, so the first peel grabs a lip instead of a feathered edge.
The printer preview shades like a lit surface instead of two flat tones.

description.p: Configurations got comfortable.

ul.li: Saving or loading a row keeps the export alive; a stale slice says so and offers to slice again.
The Layer & exposure rows put their names above the sliders, so nothing is cut off in the column.
The configuration menu lines up like a list, with markers the font can draw.

description.p: Settings can be named and called back.

ul.li: The Configuration menu by the steps saves the supports and export settings under any name, in any project.
Default stays the built-in profile; rows are removed with an × that asks first.
Switching away with changes up asks whether to update the row, save as new, or discard.
Open recent is two lists now: models and projects apart.

description.p: The preview picture is a shaded 3-D view now, the way the printer's own previews look.

ul.li: The sliced spans are stacked as solid boxes, seen from a corner above and lit from the upper left.
Both preview sizes are drawn from one span walk, a fraction of the export's own cost.
A span whose contour never closes is dropped instead of streaking across the plate.

description.p: A hollow's ceiling earns its own forest of supports.

ul.li: Coverage reaches only the slope a head belongs to, so a dome across a void grows its own columns.
Support generation is deterministic again: the island picker read candidates in hash order.
The cross-section's cut cap comes from the layer's own outlines — the texel grid is gone.

description.p: The whole face got a pass: one type scale, sentence case, and a tidier layout.

ul.li: Layer and exposure settings moved to the export tab; the slice tab keeps the cross-section view
Job files start where the project lives, or on the desktop
Layer playback runs exponentially faster than its labels say, with Loop beside the speed pills
The version shows beside the app name up top

description.p: The printer can say how much resin a print needs.

ul.li: The volume is counted off the layer masks as they are written
The weight follows at the density Creality's own numbers round to

description.p: Normal layers get their light back.

ul.li: The print parameters carry the four slots HALOT Box fills with 5, 120, 6 and 1
The exposures sit where Creality's own writer puts them
Every layer record ends in the fixed words HALOT Box writes

description.p: Files the printer is willing to read.

ul.li: Layers are laid out in the 120 byte records HALOT Box writes
The plate preview shows on the printer screen before a print
The motion settings are repeated after the pixels, as Creality does

description.p: Repeating a piece, and closing the window when it is time.

ul.li: The left strip copies a picked piece as many times as asked for
Mirror puts a mirrored copy beside it, across X, Y or Z
Quitting without saving closes the window again

description.p: Seeing the plate flat, and getting back to the usual angle.

ul.li: Persp and Ortho chips swap the lens under the viewport caption
A house under the orientation cube returns to the three-quarter view

description.p: Finding last week's plate again, and not losing this one.

ul.li: The File menu lists the last ten files that were opened or saved.
Closing the window with unsaved work asks to save, discard or stay.

description.p: Picking the piece you see, after a piece has been removed.

ul.li: Removing a piece rebuilds the drawn plate, so a click and the delete that follows act on the same piece

description.p: The layer playback got its own speed and loop controls.

ul.li: 0.5x, 1x, 2x and 4x speed buttons under the transport
A Loop switch that either starts the plate over at the top layer or stops playback there

description.p: The preset and density rows each own one number again.

ul.li: Presets change only the tip, branch, trunk and foot thicknesses
Density changes only how far apart the tips are; the two rows no longer move each other
The preset row is labelled Strut sizes so it is not mistaken for a density control

description.p: The support density control sits where it can be found, and presets agree with it.

ul.li: The Density row moved to the top Support card, directly under Preset
Presets set the density too: Light 8 mm, Medium 6 mm, Heavy 4 mm
A new plate grows about half as many supports, since the default is now 6 mm between tips

description.p: A density control for automatic supports, and fewer support columns.

ul.li: Low, Medium and High density presets on the Support tab, plus a 1.5-12 mm spacing slider
Tip spacing now sets the actual distance between supports instead of bottoming out on a fixed first-layer radius
Neighbouring tips share one trunk and foot, so a dense run no longer grows a column under every contact

description.p: Responsive slicing feedback and solid cross-sections.

ul.li: Animated working status while supports are generated, the plate is sliced, or a job is exported
Slicing runs in the background instead of freezing the window
Filled 3D cross-sections and no more hollow ball or tube supports
Opening a project no longer generates supports without being asked

description.p: Patch release for support and base geometry in exported jobs.

ul.li: Rebuild project supports automatically when a project is opened
Wait for support generation before exporting, so jobs include the support base and supports

description.p: Selection, slice-view, and control improvements.

ul.li: Progressive 3D cross-section that follows the layer slider
Responsive model highlighting with cached picking
Slice-tab 3D/Slices toggle and clearer Values dialog naming

description.p: Patch release for CXDLPv4 export compatibility.

ul.li: Quantize layer height to three decimal places so UVtools accepts the generated job file

description.p: Support-preview, slicing, and export improvements.

ul.li: 3D previews for every support setting, with a translucent model for a clear view
Reset defaults, Prepare-only transform tools, and clearer Slice and Export controls
Faster layer-mask generation and corrected HALOT-X1 CXDLPv4 output

description.p: Support-generation and model-editing reliability improvements.

ul.li: Connected cone, post, and branch geometry, including angled support junctions
Per-model support cleanup after moving, rotating, or deleting models
Uniform scaling by default, with optional independent axis scaling
